QUOTE: "By default each field is really named `private_state`, `private_flags`, and so on. Code that writes `ssl->state` against the public header fails to compile, so the field is effectively private."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members via `private_##member`, so the fields stay in the struct and only their names are broken. Hiding the layout is never mentioned.
